reason: The file-upload handle at the right edge of the Send flow is a visible, focusable icon-only button that the tree exposes as button with an empty name, on both sampled states. Enter on it opens the attachment drop zone, whose only file input is out of the Tab order, so no labelled control stands in for it. Attaching a file is optional, so the payment itself is not blocked and it stays medium.

The ellipsis button on the recipient card has an empty name and announces only as a menu button, on both sampled states. Enter opens a menu holding Edit recipient details and Pay different recipient, so a screen-reader user cannot tell what the button offers. Go back and the bank-details Edit button cover part of it, so the task is possible but hard: medium.

The Payment method field (ACH or wire) carries autocomplete="garbage" on both sampled states, and the page sets real tokens (country, address-line1, address-level1) only on fields that match an input purpose, while this field also carries data-1p-ignore, data-lpignore and data-bwignore beside the junk token. The junk token is how the page opts the field out of autofill, and the field is not one of the 53 purposes in 1.3.5.

criterionAnalysis: 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose applies to fields that collect information about the user and serve one of the 53 purposes listed in the Input Purposes section. A payment-method selector (ACH or wire, a transfer rail) is neither about the user nor one of those purposes, so there is no purpose to expose and nothing for the invalid token to break. 4.1.2 is not affected: the combobox exposes the name Payment method, role combobox and its expanded and haspopup states. No other A or AA criterion covers the autocomplete value.
